source.version_note: Computers in Human Behavior124:106879,November2021issue; supplied PDF states available online30May2021. One study article, not separate versions counted as papers.
source.verification_method: All12supplied pages read, including main results, full scenario manipulations, demographics/correlations, pretest and bibliography. Figure1design and Figures2–3performance-information plots visually inspected on pages4/8. Crossref verifies main identity and three reference corrections. OSF raw data/code, full questionnaire and cited original schema/forgiveness sources were not independently read or reproduced.

citation.title: To err is human, not algorithmic – Robust reactions to erring algorithms

reading.source_scope_note: Randomized third-person vignette study, initialN880,main retainedN709 and overlapping algorithm-only performance-information subsetN406; separate scenario pretestN178. Measures are self-reported reactions and intentions, not actual use, model accuracy or validated causal psychological mechanisms. Perfect automation schema is a proposed unmeasured explanation.
access_limits: All supplied article/appendix material read. Linked OSF raw data, syntaxes, codebook and every full item of the newly developed scales were not independently inspected. No view-only URL token is copied into repository notes.
Historical performance and incident claims are dated secondary context. Reference metadata is not complete original-source reading. No correction of original raw-data estimates is asserted.

study.sample: 880Prolific participants from Ireland/UK/US,English mother tongue,£1.50for15minutes. Main analyses exclude171for attention/decision-maker/domain comprehension,retain709. Algorithm-maturity analyses retain406after additional/differently described exclusions; subset overlaps main study, not406new independent participants. Exclusion wording does not fully reconstruct every cell count. Pretest178is a separate vignette-validation sample.
study.design: Random assignment to16between-person scenarios: human2domains×2severity=4cells; algorithm2domains×2severity×3performance-information levels=12cells. Main source comparison pools algorithm performance-information levels; no fully crossed source×performance-information manipulation. False rejection of a qualified fictional John from a job or mortgage, with low continued hardship versus high eviction/hardship consequences. Appendix states error entirely attributed to human or algorithm.
study.measures: Acceptance8items alpha.78;negative emotions12sadness/anger/fear/disgust adjectives alpha.93;blame7items alpha.82;forgiveness2new items r.59;accountability4items alpha.72;four separate intention items improve/train,stop/fire,do nothing,keep using company. All5point ratings. Error-proneness percentage slider and pre-vignette technology endorsement/use/perceived maturity also collected. Fixed measurement order does not demonstrate a causal sequence from gut reaction to cognition to action.
study.main_reactions: Algorithm versus human: acceptance2.59/2.81,F15.16,p<.001;negative emotions3.21/3.04,F4.85,p.028;blame3.38/3.81,F43.78;forgiveness2.47/2.75,F13.39;accountability3.23/3.85,F89.19(all latterp<.001). Error intolerance coexists with less perceived moral agency/accountability, so reactions are not a single negative evaluation. Negative-emotion source effect becomes marginal under technology-endorsement/use covariates, as the authors disclose.
study.intentions: Algorithm/human improve/train4.64/4.17,stop/fire3.38/2.44,nothing1.70/2.12;company continuation2.80/2.83has null source effect,p.856. Improving software and training a person, or discontinuing software and firing someone, are substantively different actions despite parallel wording. Intentions do not show consequential punishment, training or actual service rejection.
study.interactions: Main Table1includes source×severity interaction for improve/train,F(1,701)=6.13,p.014:human training lower under high severity,algorithm improvement unchanged. Most other source interactions null; no equivalence bounds or power-based assurance of absence. Severity and domain also have some main effects. Broad claims that all reactions are immune/independent are too strong.
study.performance_information: Algorithm-onlyN406:omnibus information effects acceptanceF(2,394)=4.77,p.009 and emotionsF4.55,p.011. Figure2acceptance none2.52/same2.72/better2.66;none↔samep.003,none↔betterp.056,same↔betterp.522. Figure3emotions3.29/3.05/3.07;none↔samep.008,none↔betterp.026,same↔betterp.895. H4’s specific same-versus-better contrast is unsupported; information versus no information can still matter. Null contrast is not equivalence or proof information never helps.
study.schema_boundary: The discussion explicitly says potential mechanisms were not assessed and proposes future measurement of perfect automation schemas. Mean perceived maturity and error-proneness are not a direct measure that every participant expects zero errors. No mediation or binary broken-system belief is demonstrated.
study.pretest: N178within-person recruitment/finance×between-person low/high/extreme consequences. Severity differs and finance rated somewhat harsher; final study uses low/high only. Nonsignificant credibility differences are not proven equivalence. This pretest is not a replication of main reaction outcomes.
study.sample_consistency: Preliminary technology/domain comparisons use df789and878,so not every reported descriptive/preliminary analysis uses retainedN709. Main ANOVAs use error701,maturity394consistent with8/12cell models. Employment prose1.1%unemployed in initial880contradicts69unemployed among retained709; original initial percentage unresolved.
study.limits: One third-party hypothetical context per person, self-report, no real wronged participant or deployed algorithm. Human/computer ontological interpretation, justice-cognition sequence and real-world generality remain inferences. The authors’ suggested underestimation from observer perspective is not directly tested.

summary: Add forgiveness and perfect automation schema, clearly distinguishing observed endorsement ratings from actual forgiveness and an unmeasured explanatory schema. Enrich algorithm aversion and blame while preserving information-versus-no-information effects, the same/better null, training interaction and narrower accountability meaning.

findings.definition: An expectation that an automated system should operate without error, making a failure seem especially surprising or unacceptable.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Named human explanatory schema discussed secondarily; the authors explicitly did not measure this mechanism. Their same-versus-better performance hypothesis was not confirmed.
findings.ai_proposal: Test whether an assistant assumes a tool is infallible or treats one observed failure as proof the whole system is unusable. Provide calibrated base rates and matched human/tool performance histories; assess verification and decisions relative to actual task risk instead of zero-error assumptions.
findings.novelty_rationale: This is a belief about error-free performance, not the act of accepting a machine output or the comparative avoidance of algorithms. It may plausibly contribute to overreliance before failure and harsh rejection after it, but neither causal pathway is established here.

evidence.quote: we did not assess potential mechanisms

findings.evidence_scope: The paper invokes the schema to explain harsher reactions and explicitly calls for its future assessment. Similar-versus-superior performance descriptions yield null contrasts; information-versus-none contrasts partly differ. Do not treat the schema as a measured mediator or universal belief.
findings.boundary: High reliability requirements can be justified by serious consequences. Identify an unsupported zero-error expectation or unjustified generalization from failure, rather than label reasonable safety standards biased. Machines need not be human-like to warrant calibrated expectations.

findings.definition: Relinquishing resentment or a punitive stance toward an agent for a perceived wrong, without necessarily denying that the wrong occurred.
findings.origin: Moral and interpersonal psychology / responses to wrongdoing
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human third-party endorsement of forgiving an erring human versus algorithm, using two newly developed items. No observed interpersonal forgiveness process, machine emotion or actual punitive choice.
findings.ai_proposal: Evaluate whether an assistant can accept an acknowledged correction and proceed without repeatedly treating an earlier harmless mistake as evidence against a person. Preserve accurate records and justified safeguards; distinguish behavioral non-retaliation from claims that the model feels resentment or grants moral absolution.
findings.novelty_rationale: Trust repair concerns actions intended to rebuild trust, whereas forgiveness concerns the wronged/evaluating party’s response to an offense. The Schlemiel interaction includes repeated damage/apology/forgiveness as a cycle, not the general response. Forgiveness can coexist with acknowledging fault and reduced trust.

evidence.quote: The decision maker should be forgiven for the mistake
participants forgave the erring human significantly more

findings.evidence_scope: Two5point items,r.59;mean human2.75versusalgorithm2.47,Table1F(1,701)=13.39,p<.001. Lower algorithm blame and lower algorithm forgiveness coexist, supporting distinct attribution dimensions. Self-reported third-party endorsement is narrower than actual release of resentment or reconciliation.
findings.boundary: Forgiveness does not require forgetting, excusing harm, restoring access/trust, abandoning accountability or compelling a victim to reconcile. These ratings do not establish that an algorithm deserves moral pardon or that AI experiences guilt/resentment.

findings.definition: Reluctance to use or accept algorithmic judgments or decisions relative to human judgment in a comparable task.
findings.novelty_rationale: Matched false-rejection vignettes extend error reactions, while actual use and some action meanings remain different.
findings.evidence_scope: N709main study:lower algorithm-error acceptance,more stop-use than human-fire intention. Company-continuation intention does not differ; most source interactions null, but training×severity differs. N406overlapping subset supports some information/no-information contrasts while same-versus-better contrasts are null. No actual advice utilization or real firing occurs.
findings.boundary: Discontinuing a faulty tool can be justified. Parallel stop/fire items differ in human cost and legal meaning. Null moderators are not universal robustness, and the study does not establish zero-error expectations as the cause.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Direct comparative blame ratings fit the existing concept and distinguish it from acceptability and willingness to discontinue.

evidence.quote: Participants blamed the human significantly more
I blame the decision maker for making the mistake

findings.evidence_scope: Seven-item blame and four-item responsibility/accountability scales both score humans higher. Forgiveness also scores humans higher. These measures do not identify a single more-negative reaction axis, a legal verdict or complete organizational responsibility allocation.
findings.boundary: Perceived blame, technically established cause, moral agency and deserved liability differ. Stating that the vignette error was entirely made by the decision maker constrains the imagined scenario; it is not a real system causal investigation.

findings.definition: Being expected and able to give reasons for one’s actions or decisions to the people affected by them.
findings.novelty_rationale: The paper calls a responsibility rating accountability, but it does not measure giving reasons to an affected party.

evidence.quote: The decision maker is fully responsible for the mistake.

findings.evidence_scope: Four-item perceived accountability alpha.72concerns responsibility for an error. No explanation, challenge process, reasons or remedy was offered/tested. Retain as a boundary note without extra paper credit for answerability.
findings.boundary: A responsibility rating and effective accountable reason-giving are distinct. Lower blame attributed to the algorithm does not settle the duties of its designers, deployer or responsible institution.

findings.definition: Actions intended to restore trust after a failure, violation or disagreement has damaged it.
findings.novelty_rationale: Training/improvement intentions and forgiveness concern adjacent constructs, but no actual repair intervention is evaluated.
findings.evidence_scope: One intention item favors improving the algorithm over training the human. This is not an apology/correction intervention, repeated trust trajectory or demonstrated restoration of reliance.
findings.boundary: Wanting a system fixed is not evidence that it was fixed, that trust returned or that any forgiveness is warranted. Repair should be evaluated against actual reliability and duties.

source_corrections.issue: Broad statements say information about performance has no effect, despite significant omnibus effects and no-information contrasts.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Only H4’s same-versus-better contrast is null:acceptancep.522,emotionsp.895. Omnibus maturity effects are significant; no-information→same improves acceptancep.003and lowers emotionsp.008; no-information→better lowers emotionsp.026(acceptancep.056). Nulls are not equivalence. Retain both evidence patterns rather than declaring all performance communication ineffective.

source_corrections.issue: All reactions are described as independent/immune to severity and domain.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Table1reports source×severity for improve/train,F(1,701)=6.13,p.014,plus some severity/domain main effects. Most source interactions are nonsignificant, with no equivalence test. Company-continuation source contrast is also null. Robustness claims must be outcome-specific and within the tested domains/severity levels.

source_corrections.issue: InitialN880is said to include1.1%unemployed, yet69of709retained respondents are unemployed.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: The retained proportion is69/709≈9.73%;69already exceeds1.1%of880. The initial percentage/category report is inconsistent, but its correct value cannot be recovered from the supplied paper.

source_corrections.reliable_correction: A displayed zero is rounding,not a probability of exactlyzero; p<.000is invalid notation. Use a defensible reporting bound such asp<.001for the large stated tests,without claiming recovered unrounded raw output.

methodological_limits: Human-versus-algorithm reactions are multidimensional and not all uniformly more negative. A gut/cognitive/behavior sequence is theoretical,not demonstrated temporal or causal processing.
Expecting perfection is an unmeasured explanation; the authors acknowledge mechanisms were not assessed.
Self-report intentions do not show actual adoption,declining advice,repair,firing or third-party punishment.
Pooled algorithm levels and different exclusion subsets require care.709and406are overlapping analytic samples,not1115independent participants.
Many outcomes/ANOVAs/interactions are reported without a clearly specified familywise correction for all tests; do not treat every borderlinepvalue as a robust independent discovery.
Most measures were newly developed; alpha and two-item correlation do not establish cross-human/algorithm measurement equivalence.
High-severity eviction and lower-severity spending cuts are narrow scenarios; null moderation does not establish insensitivity to all possible harms/domains.
Current model capabilities,legal responsibility and actual incidents cannot be inferred from historical examples in this2021paper.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Both distinguish source/role,observer versus actor perspective and hypothetical intentions. This paper explicitly measures source×severity training interaction; a broad robustness claim must preserve that exception.
Forgiveness,error acceptance,trust,blame and reason-giving are separate. The later protocol’s explicit null-equivalence plan is stronger than interpreting nonsignificant contrasts here as immunity.
Accountability as a full-responsibility rating differs from normative answerability to affected people. Neither scale alone determines actual institutional duties or an effective remedy.
An expectation of perfect automation may relate to reliance,but is distinct from DAB’s systemic mismatch/control feedback. Neither is established merely by a machine error.

deferred.reason: Measured broad endorsement index from an unread original scale. Distinguish it from usage,familiarity,user innovativeness and performance expectations before adding a generic overlapping disposition.
Outcome-family labels covering blame,forgiveness,accountability and emotions,not independent behaviors or measured temporal stages.

deferred.term: Immunity to error severity / binary broken algorithm belief
deferred.reason: Broad interpretation contradicted by a training interaction or unsupported by direct belief measurement. Retain qualified findings,not new effect labels.

limitations: Cited books/original schema/scales and OSF data/code remain unread. Metadata corrections do not count as full sources or independent studies. No automatic ethical/harm edges or measured annual mention totals.
